detours.why: D-666 ARM B: this B.Cu segment TERMINATES at the barrel (59.300,106.300) the same spec removes.  Relaying it between its own two ends asks the router to reach a site that is reserved and a bond that is gone; ARM A asked exactly that and got NO_PATH at 0.300 mm inside a 5.180 mm budget.  It is a stub of a removed bond, so it is REMOVED AND NOT PUT BACK and the gate's inert_removal_priced clause prices it.

note: D-667 ARM K -- ARM J under --partial, to name the pair.  Arms I and J are IDENTICAL in every routed number -- /WAKE_INT_N 35.366 mm / 5 vias, /IR_TX_GPIO16 31.822 mm / 4 vias, /SX1262_CS_N NO_PATH -- so the per-layer lane is not the constraint once the protected net is asked FIRST, and neither is the order between the two evicted nets.  /SX1262_CS_N owns three pads and therefore two MST edges, and an all-or-nothing MST aborts on the first failure and reports neither.  --partial routes every island PAIR as its own transaction, so this arm converts 'one net short' into a NAMED PAIR with a price beside it -- which is the handle the next transaction needs.  A screen: --partial can close a net's cheap edge and leave its dear one open, which is exactly what clause 4 refuses.
